cases.title: No expiry warning for certificates that expire within the warning window (known defect)
cases.intent: The run PKI's certificates are valid for 2 days (ci/e2e/lib/pki.py), well inside the default 30-day ExpirationWarningPeriod. With MutualTLS both the adapter service (server certificate and CA) and sfc-main (CA and client certificate) start a CertificateExpiryChecker, which runs once at start. It compares notAfter <= now.add(Period.ofDays(-30)), i.e. thirty days in the past, so only certificates that expired over 30 days ago would warn; these get the plain 'Checking expiration ... valid until' line instead of 'will expire in'. Correct: compare against now plus the period. IPC mode only.

knownDefect.summary: CertificateExpiryChecker tests notAfter <= now minus ExpirationWarningPeriod days, so certificates expiring within the window never warn (and the day count at :56 has the wrong sign)

cases.title: A TLS adapter service with an unusable key silently serves PlainText (known defect)
cases.intent: The adapter service is told -connection ServerSideTLS with a valid certificate but a key file that is not a key (garbage.key in this case directory). createGrpcServer catches the TLS setup exception, logs it, and builds the server without transport security; the service then announces the configured ServerSideTLS. A PlainText sfc-main gets data and the probe sees cleartext HTTP/2 on the port, so a typo in a key path silently downgrades the link. Correct: the service refuses to start. IPC mode only.

knownDefect.summary: createGrpcServer catches every TLS setup exception, logs it and returns builder.build() without transport security, and the service still logs the configured TLS connection type: an unusable key silently downgrades the service to PlainText

cases.title: A PlainText client against a TLS adapter service fails, but the dedicated mismatch hint is never logged (known defect)
cases.intent: The adapter service runs ServerSideTLS while sfc-main dials it in PlainText. No data can flow; sfc-main keeps retrying every 10 s (the case waits for the second attempt, which also proves it stays up). IpcSourceReader has a hint for exactly this misconfiguration ('PlainText connection type is configured for client, check if server requires ServerSide or Mutual TLS'), but it sits in a catch for StatusException around initializeAsync, and IpcSourceReadClient's initializer catches every exception itself and returns false. The hint is unreachable; the user gets a generic 'Failed to initialize ...' line instead. IPC mode only.

knownDefect.summary: IpcSourceReadClient's initializer swallows the StatusException and returns false, so the PlainText-versus-TLS hint in IpcSourceReader's catch (StatusException) is unreachable

cases.title: A MutualTLS adapter service serves clients that present no certificate, or one from another CA (known defect)
cases.intent: MutualTLS exists to authenticate the client. IpcBaseService builds the MutualTLS server context with trustManager(ca) but clientAuth(ClientAuth.NONE), so the server never requests a client certificate. sfc-main is a proper MutualTLS client here, so data flows whatever the fix; three probes then talk to the same port: with the CA-signed client certificate, with no certificate, and with a certificate from the unrelated rogue CA. Today all three are served HTTP/2, so anyone who can reach the port can initialise and read the adapter. Correct: only the CA-signed client is served. IPC mode only.

assert.comment: Control: the CA-signed client is served, so the probe itself works against this port.

knownDefect.summary: The MutualTLS server SslContext uses clientAuth(ClientAuth.NONE), so client certificates are never requested or verified: a client with no certificate, or with one from another CA, can initialise and read a MutualTLS adapter service

assertCurrent.comment: Served with a certificate the configured CA never signed.

cases.title: Adapter service with ServerSideTLS and a pinned server certificate delivers data encrypted
cases.intent: The adapter service is started with -connection ServerSideTLS and the run's server certificate and key, and sfc-main's server entry pins that certificate. Records flow, both sides report ServerSideTLS, and an independent probe proves the port really is TLS: the cleartext HTTP/2 preface gets no SETTINGS frame, while a TLS client that trusts only the run CA completes the handshake (ALPN h2, CN sfc-e2e-server) and is served. That proves encryption on the wire, not just configuration. IPC mode only: the IPC transport exists only there.

cases.title: ServerSideTLS without ServerCertificate works by trusting whatever certificate the server presents
cases.intent: The client side of ServerSideTLS needs no trust material: without ServerCertificate, IpcClientBuilder opens a separate TLS 1.2 connection through a trust-all X509TrustManager, takes the first certificate the server presents and pins it for the gRPC channel. sfc-main here is given no CA, no certificate and nothing else, yet records flow over a port the probe shows to be TLS-only. So the client authenticates nothing; and because the certificate is fetched again whenever the client is rebuilt (getIpcClient after every reset), it is trust on every connect, not just on first use. Undocumented; pinned as current behaviour. IPC mode only.

assert.regex: Creating client to connect to IPC service [0-9.]+:[0-9]+ using connection type ServerSideTLS

texts: Could not retrieve required server certificate

assert.comment: The port is TLS-only, so the records above crossed TLS with no client-side trust configured.

cases.title: IPC target services ignore -connection and always listen in PlainText (known defect)
cases.intent: Two file targets: FileTarget is plain IPC and carries the records gate, so the case runs the same whether or not the defect is fixed. TlsTarget's service is started exactly like a TLS adapter service (-connection ServerSideTLS -cert -key) and sfc-main is configured for ServerSideTLS with the pinned certificate. createIpcTargetServer builds its ServerConfiguration from address, port, key and cert only, and IpcTargetServerCommandLine has no connection-type accessor, so the service listens in PlainText: the probe sees cleartext HTTP/2, the TLS-configured sfc-main cannot initialise it and TlsTarget gets nothing, while target configurations (including resolved secrets) cross every target link in cleartext. Correct: the service honours -connection like adapter services do. IPC mode only.

assert.regex: Creating client to connect to IPC service [0-9.]+:[0-9]+ using connection type ServerSideTLS
assert.comment: sfc-main did dial TlsTarget with TLS.

knownDefect.summary: createIpcTargetServer builds the server configuration from address, port, key and cert only (no connection type, no CA), so every IPC target service listens in PlainText whatever -connection says; IpcMetricsServer.kt:246 has the same construction

cases.title: A MutualTLS client whose CA did not sign the server certificate is rejected
cases.intent: The adapter service runs MutualTLS with the run CA's server certificate; sfc-main has a valid client certificate but trusts only the unrelated rogue CA. The client must refuse the server: no data flows, initialisation fails with UNAVAILABLE and the read with 'General OpenSslEngine problem', and sfc-main retries after 10 s (the case waits for the second attempt, proving it stays up). CORE-IPC-TLS-MTLS-01 is the same setup with the right CA and delivers data, so the only cause is server-chain validation: the MutualTLS client does check the server, unlike the server side (CORE-IPC-TLS-MTLS-NOCLIENTCERT-01). Note the messages name no certificate problem at all. IPC mode only.
